Salicylic acid has a pKa of 2.75, meaning at pH 5, it is primarily deprotonated and negatively charged, leading to less interaction with the hydrophobic stationary phase and thus a shorter retention time. At pH 0, salicylic acid will be fully protonated and neutral, increasing its interaction with the hydrophobic stationary phase, which will increase the retention time.
